text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian neuwspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The U.S. has warned Albania not to use the army to maintain control after the recent protests against the collapse of popular pyramid schemes.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi quoted as calling the present situation unprecedented.

- Ndre Legisi, a senior member of the opposition Socialist Party, says the secret police and President Sali Berisha were to blame for the attack against him earlier this week which left him with a fractured skull.
- Students and a trades union group led by Azem Hajdari, a founder of the ruling Democratic Party, plan a demonstration to demand the resignation of the government.
- Republican Party started round table discussions on the situation but this was turned down by main opposition parties.
- President Sali Berisha said there will be no more pyramid schemes in Albania.
- Albanian lek starts to fall against hard currencies.
- Investors protest infront of the offices of two pyramid scheme companies in southern town of Gjirokaster.
- Cardinal Mikel Koliqi, 94, Albania's first Roman Catholic primate, persecuted for his faith under the former hardline communist regime and, dies after a long illness.
- A wave of arrests around the country of opposition supporters and protestors after the recent demonstrations.
- A 50-year old man hanged himself after losing everything he owned in the collapsed pyramid schemes.
- Council of Europe to discuss the Albanian crisis.
- Mario Kempes, Argentine World Cup winner and currently coach of Lushnje soccer team, asked permission to leave the country until the situation returns to normal.
